title: Briefing: India, Albania, Canada, Italy and France
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Saturday, October thirty-first. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means only one source has it so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.
In India, Cockroach Janta Party president Abhijeet Dipke posted an Instagram note to singer Diljit Dosanjh asking to end their row, News18 and Hindustan Times report.
In Albania, the government presented its 2027 tax package, cutting food VAT while raising the standard rate, Tirana Times reports.
In Canada, Imperial Oil's chief executive said he is encouraged by progress toward a binding Pathways carbon-storage agreement, BNN Bloomberg reports.
In Italy, tens of thousands marched in Rome and Milan against the cost of living and military spending, NBC News reports.
In France, the interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide over the cost of living, Al Jazeera reports.

In India, singer Diljit Dosanjh answered critics of his June remark at his Delhi tour opening, Deccan Chronicle reports. We grade that reported: it rests on one source so far, not yet independently confirmed.

In Albania, the government presented its 2027 tax package on October twenty-eighth, dropping an earlier plan to raise corporate income tax and cutting VAT on 54 basic foods, Tirana Times reports. Our grade: reported, because so far only Tirana Times has it, and we are waiting for independent confirmation.

In Canada, Imperial Oil's chief executive said he is encouraged by progress toward a binding Pathways carbon-storage agreement with Ottawa and Alberta, a condition for the Pacific Link pipeline, BNN Bloomberg reports. Our grade: reported, resting on one source, BNN Bloomberg, and not yet confirmed by a second. British Columbia's Conservative Party won a majority government in the snap election Premier David Eby called for October twenty-four, CTV News declares. Our grade for the election win is confirmed, with independent reporting from CBC and CTV.

In Italy, tens of thousands marched in Rome and Milan on Friday against the cost of living and military spending, NBC News reports. Our grade: reported, as so far only NBC News has it, and we are waiting for independent confirmation.

In France, the interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris, in marches over the cost of living, Al Jazeera reports. Our grade: reported, resting on one source, Al Jazeera, and not yet confirmed by a second.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
